diagnostic_evidence.quote: the operation $\{H,\cdot\}$ is a derivation of $C^\infty(M)$, so it is a vector field, denoted by $X_H$
Then we can transport the original Hamilton function $H(x)$ to the homogeneous Poisson manifold considering $H^P(x,t) = tH(x)$.
describe a Hamiltonian vector field $X^P_H$ on $P$ inducing the same dynamics on $J$ as $X_H$

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's Poisson convention (X_F := {F,.} = Pi(dF,.) on the Poissonization), a direct computation for t-independent g gives X^P_{tH}(g) = Pi(d(tH),dg) = Lambda(dH,dg) + H E(g). Hence the Hamiltonian vector field of the lift H^P = tH projects to g |-> Lambda(dH,dg) + HE(g), which is exactly minus the paper's Jacobi Hamiltonian vector field X_H(g) = Lambda(dg,dH) - HE(g); the latter is also minus the derivation part of the paper's own Jacobi bracket {H,g}_J = Lambda(dH,dg) + HE(g) - gEH. Thus the lifted dynamics induces -X_H on J, not X_H, contradicting the stated plan that X^P_H induce the same dynamics as X_H.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define X_H = Lambda(dH,.) + HE(.) (the derivation part of {H,.}_J); the adjacent remark then becomes that E is the Hamiltonian vector field of the constant function 1. With this single overall sign correction, tau_* X^P_{tH} = X_H and the construction is consistent.
issues.overall_effect: The entire JHI construction of Section 6 as written approximates the time-reversed flow of the intended Jacobi Hamiltonian vector field; the claimed correspondence between hPHI for H^P = tH and JHI for H^J is off by a sign.
issues.title: Jacobi Hamiltonian vector field defined with the wrong overall sign, so the Poissonized lift integrates -X_H
issues.why_classification: One forced overall sign correction in a single displayed formula (repeated once) plus the adjacent remark; after it, every structural claim of the paper is preserved with no new argument or weakening.

issues.failure_explanation: For h_z(x,t) = (x,zt), pushforward gives (h_z)_*(\partial_t) = z\partial_t and (h_z)_*((1/t)Lambda(x)) = (z/t)Lambda(x), hence (h_z)_*Pi = z Pi (equivalently L_{t\partial_t}Pi = -Pi). So under the paper's definition of k-homogeneity for multivector fields, (h_z)_*X = z^kX, the Poissonization is (+1)-homogeneous and fails the -1-homogeneity required by the Definition of homogeneous Poisson manifold; the displayed computation in the proof is false as written, and the definition excludes the paper's own central construction. The standard convention, which the paper's later spray computations in fact use, is the pullback one h_z^*pi = z^{-1}pi, under which the claim is correct.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Measure multivector homogeneity by pullback ((h_{z^{-1}})_*X = z^kX, i.e. h_z^*X = z^kX) instead of pushforward in (vf k-homoge), and adjust the display accordingly; then Pi is indeed -1-homogeneous and all later, convention-free (0-homogeneity/invariance) arguments are untouched.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the Poissonization is not a homogeneous Poisson manifold in the paper's own sense, so the hPHI framework of Section 6 formally lacks its object; the proof display of prop:added-1 is false.
issues.title: Poissonization bivector is not -1-homogeneous under the paper's pushforward convention (it is +1-homogeneous)
issues.why_classification: Forced local convention/sign repair in the definition and one displayed claim; every subsequent use concerns invariance (0-homogeneity), which is convention-independent, so no claim is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed Pi has coefficient of \partial_t\wedge\partial_z equal to -1, i.e. pi^{tz} = -1 and pi^{zt} = +1, in agreement with the paper's own homogeneity analysis (pi^{vt} = -E_v with E_z = -1). Formula (eq: approximation alpha) applied to this Pi forces alpha^t = t + (1/2)pi^{zt}xi_z = t + (1/2)xi_z, but the example displays t - (1/2)xi_z (and, consistently via beta(y,xi) = alpha(y,-xi), beta^t = t + (1/2)xi_z in (eq: bi-realization example2)). The first three components of alpha follow (eq: approximation alpha) while the t-component follows the opposite sign (the spray half-flow), so the displayed map is not, in all components, the stated order-2 truncation of the realization of the displayed Pi.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the t-components by alpha^t = t + (1/2)xi_z and beta^t = t - (1/2)xi_z, matching (eq: approximation alpha) applied to the displayed Pi.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's only explicit example of a homogeneous bi-realization is internally inconsistent; it is illustrative and no later proof depends on it.
issues.title: Sign error in the t-component of the displayed order-2 bi-realization example
issues.why_classification: A one-term sign correction in an example with no dependents; no other claim or construction is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: in that case we call variation functions to any time-dependent functions $(f_s)_{s\in I}$ such that $df_s = \xi_s$, for all $s\in I$.

issues.failure_explanation: Variation functions are arbitrary primitives of xi_s. The direction (f_s 1-homogeneous => xi_s = df_s 1-homogeneous) holds, but the converse fails because primitives may be modified by 0-homogeneous functions. Concrete counterexample: on P = R^\times with h_z(t) = zt, xi = dt is a 1-homogeneous exact 1-form, and f = t + 1 is a primitive that is not 1-homogeneous. What is true (and what the later construction uses) is that 1-homogeneous closed xi_s admit a 1-homogeneous primitive, e.g. f_s = i_Z xi_s, since L_Z xi_s = xi_s implies d(i_Z xi_s) = xi_s.

failure_location.quote: Then $\xi_s$ are $1$-homogeneous if and only if $f_s$ are $1$-homogeneous.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate as: xi_s are 1-homogeneous if and only if the variation functions can be chosen 1-homogeneous (the choice is then unique, since two primitives differ by a locally constant, hence 0-homogeneous, function, which must vanish to be 1-homogeneous).
issues.overall_effect: The stated equivalence is false; only the existence of homogeneous variation functions (which survives) supports the integrator construction.
issues.title: Corollary cor:added-1: 'if and only if' is false in one direction for arbitrary variation functions
issues.why_classification: The repair is a restatement to the existence form actually used downstream; no argument or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's ambient form Omega = pr_1^*omega - pr_2^*omega on T^*Q x T^*Q and its convention omega(X_H,.) = dH, definition (eq: variation form) gives, for u = (v, T phi^t_H v) in TG^t_H: xi_t(u) = Omega((0, X_H), u) = -omega(X_H, T phi^t_H v) = -(Phi^{-t*}_H dH)(u). So the variation form of G^t_H is -Phi^{-t*}_H dH, not +Phi^{-t*}_H dH as claimed. The invocation of Proposition prop: two symplectic lagrangian is also formally inapplicable, since the identification Phi^{-t}_H is t-dependent while the proposition concerns a single fixed symplectomorphism.

failure_location.quote: By Example \ref{ex: dH}, the variation form in $T^*Q$ is $dH$ so, using Proposition \ref{prop: two symplectic lagrangian}, the variation form of $G^t_H$ is $\Phi^{-t*}_HdH.$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the variation form as -Phi^{-t*}_H dH (with the paper's conventions), or derive it directly from (eq: variation form) instead of via Proposition prop: two symplectic lagrangian.
issues.overall_effect: A sign error in the heuristic bridge identifying flow-graphs with Hamilton-Jacobi generating families in Section 5.2; together with the sign error in (eq: H-J), the variation-form correspondence there is inconsistent with the paper's conventions.
issues.title: Variation form of the flow-graph family G^t_H has the wrong sign
issues.why_classification: Local sign correction in an unlabeled illustrative example; no labeled result depends on it and the repair is immediate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: when $L \xhookrightarrow{} (\Sigma,\omega)$ is a Lagrangian bisection for $R$, the induced map $\varphi_L = \beta\circ \alpha^{-1}_{|L}$ defines a Poisson diffeomorphism $(P,\Pi)\rightarrow (P,\Pi)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The quoted theorem guarantees only in item (1) that varphi_L is a Poisson diffeomorphism; Hamiltonian flows arise from the specific bisections L_s = phi^s_{alpha^*H}(sigma(P)) (item 3), or more generally from exact families. In the paper's own pair-groupoid example of Section 5.3, Lagrangian bisections are graphs of symplectomorphisms, and a general symplectomorphism (e.g. a translation on a torus) is not the time-1 flow of any Hamiltonian. So the sentence claims more than the theorem provides.

failure_location.quote: Theorem \ref{thm: ham flow} guarantees that, given a Lagrangian bisection $L$, the induced diffeomorphism $\varphi_L$ is a Hamiltonian flow.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'is a Hamiltonian flow' by 'is a Poisson diffeomorphism' (or explicitly restrict the claim to exact families of bisections).
issues.overall_effect: A false gloss of the cited key theorem; the immediately following sentence restricts to exact families with L_0 the zero section, where the needed conclusion holds, so the actual construction is unaffected.
issues.title: Prose misstates Theorem thm: ham flow: a general Lagrangian bisection induces a Poisson diffeomorphism, not necessarily a Hamiltonian flow
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence prose correction; the construction that follows already uses the correct stronger hypothesis, so nothing downstream is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consider also the Poincar\'{e}-Cartan 1-form $\eta_{PC}= p_idq^i - Hdt$.
p_i = \frac{\partial F_1}{\partial q^i},\quad P_i = -\frac{\partial F_1}{\partial Q^i},\quad K = H - \frac{\partial F_1}{\partial t}.

issues.failure_explanation: Preserving d eta_{PC} with the paper's own eta_{PC} = p_idq^i - Hdt (and eta'_{PC} = P_idQ^i - Kdt) requires p_idq^i - Hdt - P_idQ^i + Kdt = dF_1, but the paper writes p_idq^i + Hdt - (P_idQ^i + Kdt) = dF_1, flipping the signs of both dt-terms (and thereby failing its stated goal of leaving d eta_{PC} unchanged). From the mis-signed identity the paper obtains K = H - \partial_t F_1 instead of the correct K = H + \partial_t F_1, and imposing K = 0 yields (eq: H-J), H(q, \partial_q S_t, t) = \partial_t S_t, whereas the correct Hamilton-Jacobi equation is \partial_t S_t + H(q, \partial_q S_t, t) = 0. Solutions of the displayed equation generate the time-reversed Hamiltonian dynamics.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the identity to p_idq^i - Hdt - (P_idQ^i - Kdt) = dF_1, giving K = H + \partial_t F_1, and replace (eq: H-J) by \partial_t \mathbf{S}_t + H(q, \partial_q \mathbf{S}_t, t) = 0.
issues.overall_effect: The Hamilton-Jacobi equation used throughout Section 5.2 to build the Lagrangian bisections for the integrator has the wrong sign; the resulting generating functions correspond to -H rather than H.
issues.title: Homogeneous Hamilton-Jacobi equation (eq: H-J) has the wrong sign
issues.why_classification: The defect is a sign in one labeled equation and the preceding unlabeled identity; the forced repair is a local sign flip and every structural claim survives.
